C2_shared_claim_values.why: each part's preimage is solved to meet the value the CAPTURE carries, so a value two commitments both publish is met as the same number by both.  A shared value is a coupling that costs nothing; a shared UNKNOWN is the one that costs everything (C1)

So the masking commitment and the 23 sumchecks are met by ONE coefficient vector per stage, not by two independent solves

C4_the_terminal_identity.what_can_be_said: every quantity the identity relates -- fin_s, c_s, mask_eval_s and the terminals -- is a PUBLISHED number, and this assignment reproduces every published number of the run exactly.  So the identity holds at the reproduced view for the trivial reason that the reproduced view IS the captured view, entry by entry.  That is NOT the same as saying the assignment is a witness of the identity's arithmetic: the terminals are met as claim VALUES by blinding, and whether a model input exists whose activations make them is a question about the block's arithmetic that no preimage argument answers (round 7 §11.8, second bullet)

channels.channel: the hash RULE of the run: which BLAKE3 made every byte, and the four keys of a tagged profile
channels.derivation: the four context strings and the list of legacy profiles are pinned in the gate's own source, the key set is DERIVED from the profile the bundle's shape names (the port of Shape::hash_tag) and compared with the bundle's declared hash_tag member by member -- re-derive, never consume (ruling T-7).  The bytes are then shown to be under that rule: the whole transcript replays, and every opened column re-hashes and re-authenticates, only under it
channels.keys_are_public: yes -- each key is blake3.derive_key(<public context>, <public profile>), so publishing them discloses nothing; they are never an INPUT

channels.channel: the Merkle roots (A, H, M and the two endpoint roots)
channels.model_assumption: the roots are generated by the prover itself (ruling D18) and indistinguishability rests on M-2, the hiding of unopened salted leaves in the random-oracle model.  A boundary root is an observed commitment and NOT part of the run statement
channels.what_stage_9_adds_and_what_it_does_not: stage 9 re-hashes every OPENED column and folds its path to the root under the rule, so the root is COMPUTED from the opened data rather than read -- a soundness-side check.  The channel stays ARGUED because what it is about is HIDING: what an unopened leaf reveals is M-2's assumption either way

channels.channel: leaf salts
channels.model_assumption: fresh uniform bytes in both worlds; equality of the two laws rests on M-3, the assumption that the whole output stream of ZkRng is indistinguishable from uniform

channels.channel: authentication paths
channels.model_assumption: the paths are genuine hashes of the same world's own columns; hiding of the unopened leaf digests rests on M-2.  That they ARE genuine hashes of this run's own columns is now computed, not assumed (stage 9), including each path's LENGTH against the tree depth -- the check that stops an inner node being presented as a salted leaf

channels.channel: the receipt frame: its one length and its 40-byte envelope
channels.model_assumption: a standalone block's receipt is ONE frame, with no segment and no position tag.  Its length is the shape's counted receipt length, a function of the shape and not of the witness -- EVIDENCE, not proof: the dense and the all-zero bundles' frames have the same length.  Its 40-byte envelope is the magic HLPBLOK1 and block_binding (wire.rs:15, :145-146), compared by stage 1 with the binding stage 2 RECOMPUTES from the public header words, and outside the Fiat-Shamir chain

channels.channel: the joint law of the block's view beyond the linear rank
channels.reason: what is computed here is a RANK of a linear model over the block's five commitments.  The joint LAW of one shaped block's view is Theorem B's per-stage part -- the toy theorem at a shaped layout -- written and accepted as a REDUCTION (joint-law composition disposition, 2026-09-20 17:58, section 1), conditional on G-R1, G-R2 and G-R4.  The draw accounting ruling R-3 asked for is machine-asserted on single-block proofs at six shapes (lane stage 36), not at 125M
channels.ruling_R3: ruling R-3: `joint == sum of the parts` is a CONSISTENCY CHECK of this model's coordinate classes, NOT evidence that the commitments' blinding is independent.  The checker built the counterexample: two DISTINCT blinding rows whose VALUES coincide score exactly like an honest run (joint 0 = sum 0) while disclosing 1,024 field elements at this shape.  Independence across the 4L+1 commitments rests on the generator and the draw discipline (gap G-R4), is to be machine-asserted elsewhere, and is not established by anything in this figure
channels.ruling_R3_as_of_2026_09_23: 2026-09-23 (round 9j): the draw-accounting test ruling R-3 asked for EXISTS -- lane stage 36, the seven assertions of ZK60_JOINT_SENTENCE_AND_QUERY_CLASSES.md section 3.1, MEASURED on single-block proofs at six shapes (toy, rung-K4, rung-P2, rung-C6, rung-W14, rung-E32).  Not at 125M, where the per-block draw total is a count, and not at run scope (J-5's widened assertion 2 over 11L + 3(L-1) segments is unmeasured).  `joint == sum` in this gate remains a consistency check of the model, as the ruling says
channels.section: block (replaces the run's cross-block joint law)

channels.channel: the preimage construction for the BLOCK (one randomness reproducing the whole block's view under a fixed input)
channels.reason: exhibited PER COMMITMENT for all 4 PCS commitments of the run, both halves, every opened column and their salted leaves (round 7).  It is still not a RUN preimage: a run preimage is a JOINT object -- one randomness reproducing every stage's view at once with each boundary plane shared between three commitments -- and round 7's control P-5 is exactly the case where per-commitment preimages exist and no joint one does.  The CFS channel is unconstructed as well
channels.section: block (replaces the run's preimage for a RUN)

channels.assumption: D12 item 5 as pinned: IoSpec::new and ruling CS-8 refuse any endpoint scale pair but ENDPOINT_SCALES
channels.channel: the endpoint scales and the one calibration identity
channels.model_assumption: a standalone block has no boundary and no interior scale.  Its two endpoint scales are words of the endpoint policy, a CONSTANT of the approved calibration (private_block.rs:371, ENDPOINT_SCALES = (0, 0); IoSpec::new refuses any other pair and ruling CS-8 re-checks it at every entry), so they carry nothing about the hidden input.  What the gate COMPUTES: the policy bytes the header absorbs (expected-IO) are parsed and carry exactly the declared context, scales and roots, the scales are the approved pair, and the ONE calibration identity is absorbed -- the header binding reproduces over it
channels.section: block (replaces the run's boundary scale tags)

channels.channel: whether a proof attempt produced a receipt (refusal events)
channels.reason: the refusal channel is inside the game (ruling C-2); a capture exists only when the block was accepted.  Its ENTROPY side is three fail-closed operating-system reads per proof: the block prover's one generator in prove_inner_at ('ONE OS stream per attempt; entropy failure aborts before anything public exists', seeded from hash_domain::single_block_seed_domain) and one in each of the two endpoint owners (endpoint_g.rs:269) -- lane stage 36's clarification 5, asserted as a source fact, and J-2.  A lookup miss is ONE named refusal before the first commitment (ruling CS-3), whose text names only the table family
